sentences: The first version worked on my machine, which is exactly why it needed a second look.
A small, boring change removed most of the noise and made the failures easy to reproduce.
Measure first: the slowest part was never the part I would have guessed.
Keep the happy path short and give every failure a name you can search for.
Defaults matter more than options, because most people never change them.
Write the test that fails for the right reason before touching the code.
The cheapest monitoring is a health endpoint that checks the one thing that breaks.
Logs are for people at 3 a.m.: say what happened, to what, and what to try next.
Prefer a plain table and a clear index over a clever abstraction you must explain.
Ship the smallest slice that proves the idea, then widen it with evidence.
